/LILIAN

Baltic Exchange Market Report 17 June 2026
Baltic Dry Index: 2653 (-17)
Baltic Capesize Index: 3877 (-34)
Baltic Panamax Index: 2223 (-43)
Baltic Supramax Index: 1705 (20)
Baltic Handysize Index: 917 (7)
CAPESIZE
The market softened marginally with the BCI 5TC easing $309 to settle at $35,162. The C5 index remained broadly flat, edging up just $0.020 to $10.730, while C3 came under more pronounced pressure, declining $0.859 to $31.750. The Pacific was the brighter of the two basins, with healthy cargo volumes and a noticeable increase in coal stems from East Coast Australia helping to lift sentiment. There was a growing feeling amongst market participants that the market may have found a floor. Two of the major C5 miners were active, contributing to a firmer undertone as the day progressed. Early fixtures saw a Newcastlemax reported at $10.50, followed by another miner fixing multiple times at $10.80 and $10.85, before an operator pushed the market slightly higher, concluding at $11.00. Conversely, the Atlantic basin continued to show signs of weakness, with sentiment softer amid limited visible activity. South Brazil and West Africa to China remained under pressure, with the C3 spread narrowing somewhat compared to the previous session, although bids were still reported around the $30.00 level versus $32–33 for index dates.
PANAMAX
Brokers reported that Atlantic activity softened today following a more active session yesterday, particularly on trans Atlantic routes. While the overall Atlantic market appears fairly balanced, sources noted that prompt tonnage opening in the North Continent remains tight. As a result, sources highlight the potential that certain fixtures may achieve short term premiums above prevailing market levels depending on loading windows. In the Pacific, sentiment continues to trend weaker, with charterers showing limited urgency and overall activity remaining subdued. A persistent bid-offer gap is evident, with brokers reporting that some owners are still reluctant to fully align their ideas with current bid levels. The P5TC index declined by $384 today to settle at $20,009.

Atlantic
The Golden Frigo (84,520 2024) open Hamburg 20 June was said to have been placed on subjects for a US East Coast trip with coal to the Continent at $22,500 to Panagea.

Asia
Oldendorff were reported to have taken the Guo Yuan 26 (75,855 2012) open in Campha 25 June for a trip with clinker to the Ivory Coast at $19,000. An unknown charterer was said to have covered their 70,000/10 coal stem on a TBN basis, loading Kaliorang and discharging in Navlakhi for 19/24 June at $15.70.
SUPRAMAX
The market appeared to be trending sideways as the week passed the midway stage. The major increase in the 11TC was S1B fuelled by yesterdays reported trades, but otherwise the market appeared relatively flat. The Asian market remained cautious despite potential progress in a Hormuz Strait agreement. The 11TC average today rose $254 to settle at $21,558.

Atlantic
The North Americas remained active with the Desert Leopard (63,569 2025) said to be placed on subjects from New Orleans 30 June for a trip to UK-Continent with grains at $31,750 with Bunge. Refined Success reportedly placed the S-Bond (58,097 2012) on subjects basis SW Pass 1/2 July for a trip to WC Central America-WC South America with grains at $32,000. There were further rumours of an Ultramax fixing inter-gulf at $28,000 whilst a 58,000-dwt agreed at $25,500 for a similar trade, a 61,000-dwt fixing SW Pass to Singapore-Japan at $32,000 and a 60,000-dwt fixed at $27,000 for SW Pass to North Coast South America. Further East the Belgrace (63,718 2024) fixed a scrap cargo from Rotterdam for discharge East Mediterranean at $26,000 with Norden.

Asia
There was talk of a 64,000-dwt being placed on subjects from North China for a trip to West Africa at $25,500 but further details were lacking. In the Indian Ocean the Themistocles (55,793 2014) open South Africa 26/30 June was fixed by Oldendorff for a trip Singapore-Japan with some reports suggesting the rate was $23,000 plus $230,000 ballast bonus, whilst others thought it was $22,000 plus $220,000. Likewise there was a difference of opinion on the rate the Kiran Istanbul (63,610 2013) agreed from Zanzibar via Port Elizabeth intention manganese ore to China with Pacific Basin with initial reports of $25,000 later being corrected to $26,000.
HANDYSIZE
The market continued to deliver a mixed performance, with some regions holding steady while others recorded modest gains. The BHSI edged up by 7 points to 917, while the 7TC average rising by $117 to $16,502. Across the Continent and Mediterranean, only marginal adjustments were observed, with rates remaining largely unchanged. In the South Atlantic and US Gulf, market views were generally positive, with sources noting that rate gains were primarily driven by stronger demand and tighter tonnage; overall, the market remained firm. Asian markets were more subdued, as reduced cargo enquiry and softer activity contributed to a mild downward drift in rates. On the period side, the Devbulk Servet (39,830 2020) was fixed delivery passing Coatzacoalcos for a minimum of 4 and about 6 months at $18,500, although further details were not disclosed.

Atlantic
The Ricarda (39,949 2015) was reported fixed for a trip delivery Santos to the Continent in the $23,000s. Another Handysize was heard fixed for a trip delivery West Africa via Santos to the West Mediterranean at around $16,000–$17,000, although further details were not disclosed.

Asia
The An Hai Vincent (30,634 2007), open Kaohsiung on 25 June, was placed on subjects for a North Vietnam to Arabian Gulf trip, with intention Fujairah or Oman, carrying aluminium ore in the $20,000s, although further details were lacking.

Market Fundamentals
Roy Hill to cut output, extend mine life by decade

Hancock will cut production at its Roy Hill iron ore mine in Western Australia's Pilbara region to extend the mine's lifespan by a decade, the company said on 17 June. Mining activity will be reduced, though output will be maintained above 63 Mtpa. The updated mine plan aims to maximise orebody recovery and reduce waste mined. With a current lifespan of 20 years, Roy Hill, which produced its first shipment in 2015, shipped 61.6 Mt in FY2025, despite record rainfall and disruption from tropical cyclone Zelia, according to the company. ai_analysis.summary: 17日干散货市场分化运行，BDI下跌17点至2653。Capesize与Panamax承压走弱，BCI 5TC跌309美元至35162美元，C3航线跌破32美元；Supramax与Handysize逆势走强，BSI反弹254美元。FFA市场看跌情绪浓厚，Cape与Pmx各月份合约全线下跌，Jul合约领跌。太平洋市场相对活跃，C5触底迹象显现，大西洋延续疲态。

sections.title: Market Structure
sections.content: Capesize与Panamax指数回落，C3大西洋端压力加大，南美-中国降至30美元附近。Supramax和Handysize指数小幅走强，跨大西洋航线HS3领涨544点。太平洋市场情绪回暖，C5触底信号初现，C5TC前端仍具韧性。FFA前端合约跌幅扩大，Jul合约抛压明显，市场对短期运价预期转向悲观。

sections.title: Dry Bulk Signals
sections.content: Capesize前端企稳迹象：C5两大矿商活跃，Newcastlemax有$11.00成交，太平洋情绪好转。大西洋持续承压：C3维持$30-31区间，南美出口需求疲弱。Supramax S1B航线暴涨1333点，受昨日成交推动；USG至Skaw航线S4A涨286点至32879美元。Handysize跨大西洋航线HS3大涨544点，南美出口支撑明显。

sections.title: Trading Focus
sections.content: 关注C3进一步走向：当前$30水平能否形成支撑，若进一步跌破$30则Cape跌势或延续。C5前端可逢低关注：矿商活跃度回升，$10.80-11.00区间成交密集，太平洋基本面尚可。FFA Jul Pmx空头可继续持有，目标$19000；Cape Jul维持偏空但注意$28000一线支撑。跨大西洋回空航线S4B暴涨621点至12414美元，可关注空放机会。

market_watch: C3 South Brazil-China徘徊$30-31.75，跌破$30将加剧Cape下行压力
FFA Cape Jul 26合约跌破$28500关键支撑，趋势转弱
Supramax S1B航线暴涨1333点，受益于中东-中国货盘活跃
Handysize HS3 Rio-Skaw大涨544点，南美粮食出口支撑大西洋市场
Pmx前端合约全线走弱，Jul跌至$19750，20日均线已失守

route_focus.view: 大西洋端持续承压，South Brazil至China维持$30-31区间，C3价差收窄。虽有$30水平报价，但需求疲弱，短期缺乏反弹动力，预计仍将在$30-32区间波动。
Capesize 5TC index今日跌309至35162美元。太平洋市场情绪回暖，Newcastlemax成交$10.85-11.00，$10.80有重要支撑；大西洋端疲弱。指数整体仍处高位，但趋势偏弱。
Skaw-Passero至Rio-Skaw航线（HS3）大涨544点至22922美元，南美粮食出口旺季支撑大西洋市场。US Gulf至Skaw航线（HS4）涨271点至20146美元，跨大西洋运力趋紧。预计短期继续走强。
